title: Full-column-rank least squares: relative prediction error

model.instance: The unknown matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$ has full column rank, with $m\ge n$ and $\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}\le\kappa$. Inputs $b\in\mathbb R^m,x_0\in\mathbb R^n$ are public.

assumptions.description: Full column rank, with κ(A) = σ_max/σ_min ≤ κ.

metric.normalization: Error is relative to the initial least-squares excess, excess=||A(x-x*)||_2². Zero initial excess requires exact success.

metric.description_zh: The loss is $\ell(\widehat x)=\|A(\widehat x-x^\star)\|_2^2/\|A(x_0-x^\star)\|_2^2$ and must satisfy $\ell\le\varepsilon$. A zero denominator requires an exact solution. applicability.metric_and_probability_mapping: Take $\delta_0=\eta_0=1/2$ in the source Theorem 2.8, with sufficient dimension $n\ge C\kappa^{13}$. Use its symmetric invertible hard matrix $n\times n$ as a consistent least-squares instance and set $x_0=0$. If $m>n$, append zero rows to the matrix and right-hand side. This preserves full column rank, the singular-value condition number, and the cost of both query directions. The loss is exactly $\|A\widehat x-b\|_2^2/\|b\|_2^2$, so $\varepsilon\le n^{-2}$ implies the source residual threshold $1/n$. Three independent repetitions, each followed by one right product to check the residual, raise success probability from $2/3$ to $26/27$. The original budget is therefore at least $c\kappa\log n-O(1)$. In the strip $n^{-4}\le\varepsilon\le n^{-2}$, the normal-equation CG upper bound $O(\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon))$ matches it. This does not establish a fixed-small-dimension optimum.

proofs.title: Deterministic CG on the normal equations, charging two calls per AᵀA product.
proofs.body:
Let $B=A^{\mathsf T}A$ and $x^\star=B^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b$. Full column rank makes $B$ positive definite, with $\kappa(B)=\kappa(A)^2\le\kappa^2$. Form the initial normal-equation residual $A^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax_0)$ using one right and one transpose product; a zero residual identifies the exact least-squares minimizer. Each subsequent $Bv$ uses one product with $A$ and one with $A^{\mathsf T}$.
CG gives
$$\|x_t-x^\star\|_B^2\le4\left(\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}\right)^{2t}\|x_0-x^\star\|_B^2.$$
Because $\|e\|_B^2=\|Ae\|_2^2$, the ratio is exactly the declared excess least-squares loss, including inconsistent systems. It is not relative total fitting residual. Choose $t=O(\kappa\log(4/\varepsilon))$. The implementation uses $t+1$ calls in each channel. Enlarging the universal ceiling constant absorbs initialization and gives the registered scalar form $1+2\lceil C\kappa\log(4/\varepsilon)\rceil$. In a joint-budget statement, take the displayed iteration allowance at least one larger than the number of CG updates; both actual channel counts then satisfy the recorded upper allowances. Exact arithmetic and public-data processing are uncharged.

proofs.title: Deterministic reconstruction using the standard basis, followed by free exact solution of the target task
proofs.body: Query the $n$ standard basis vectors of $\mathbb R^n$ to recover the full rectangular matrix $A$. Full column rank makes $(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b$ the unique least-squares minimizer, even if $Ax=b$ is inconsistent. Exact internal linear algebra is uncharged, and the excess loss is zero. The joint query budget is $(n,0)$.
